newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares close higher, pulled by Germany.
newsitem.headline: French shares close higher, pulled by Germany.

text.p: French shares closed higher on Tuesday, pulled by a rally in German shares which in turn was powered by a banking merger, dealers said.
A higher start on Wall Street, with gains of over 50 points in early trading, and a firmer dollar also helped.
Brokers said there was also a lot of short covering buying from people who had taken a position ahead of the announcement of the French corporate tax rises on Monday.
The CAC-40 index closed up 47.01, or 1.64 percent, at 2,921.13. CAC-40 July futures ended at 2,930 vs 2,885 at Monday's close.
The broader SBF120 index was up 28.3 at 1,996.94.
Volume was 8.5 billion francs of which seven billion in CAC-40 shares.
Renault biggest riser with six percent gain to 164.80 francs after J.P. Morgan issues a buy advice.
"Sellers who were short before the audit and tax measures had to buy back quickly because the futures market and the dollar rose quickly," said a dealer about the overall stockmarket market.

"The rise in the dollar or the fall in interest rates (on the bond market) has far more weight than the rise in taxes. The dollar leverage is very important for some companies," said Pierre Vignaud at EIFB.
Vignaud, a technical analyst, said he expected the market to continue its rise and reach the 2,950 level in the short term.
The all-time high for the index is at 3,006.54 set on July 17.

Other dealers and investors were more cautious ahead of a speech by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan to congress. Greenspan's "irrational exuberance" comment about stock markets in December caused a slide in prices.
* The banking sector was in play following a German merger with BNP up 1.22 percent at 249.60 francs, Societe Generale up 3.94 percent at 738 and Paribas up 1.11 percent at 402.40.
* Credit Lyonnais was 5.72 percent higher at 308.70 francs, also helped by talks the government may be close to handing its privatisation dossier to the European Union commission in Brussels.
* Lafarge, up 4.74 percent at 398 francs, boosted by results of Lafarge Corp.
